standard.title: Analyse and evaluate information in texts
standard.description: analyse and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information across text types, evaluate sources, and respond analytically and personally (AC9LCH8EC03). They have applied comprehension strategies and produced structured responses. They have not yet evaluated information using rhetorical and analytical frameworks, created formal responses to contemporary issues, or analysed entertainment texts for their relationship to social issues.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a range of texts — including rhetorical analysis, source evaluation with citation, and formal responses to contemporary issues.

nodes.label: Rhetorical and analytical text analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how language conveys meaning in texts — including rhetorical questions, irony, sarcasm, and persuasive technique — and evaluate key messages in contemporary target language media.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two rhetorical or persuasive techniques in a target language text and explain how each conveys meaning or influences the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate key messages in magazines, newspapers, websites and podcasts for Chinese-speaking students; analyse how rhetorical questions, irony and sarcasm work in texts; analyse entertainment texts for their relationship to contemporary issues; identify language that influences reader response.
wider: Compare how persuasive technique is used in target language and English media on the same contemporary issue — identify differences in rhetoric and discuss what they reveal about audience expectations
Produce a rhetorical analysis of a published target language text — identify every persuasive or rhetorical device with metalanguage and evaluate the text's overall effectiveness
nodes.hinge_reason: Rhetorical analysis is the prerequisite for all critical text work at Y9-10. Students who can only retrieve information cannot evaluate how meaning is constructed and cannot produce the analytical responses the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Rhetorical analysis requires an explicit framework — students need to know what to look for (rhetorical questions, irony, evidence use, framing) before they can identify and evaluate these features. Explicit analytical framework instruction followed by guided practice builds this capacity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two rhetorical or persuasive techniques in a text
Explains how each technique conveys meaning or influences the reader

nodes.label: Evaluating sources and citing references
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate print and digital sources for reliability, gather information from a range of sources, and reference them appropriately in target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two sources for reliability using explicit criteria, gather information from both, and cite at least one source appropriately in target language.
nodes.typical_width: Access digital and print texts to research current affairs; evaluate sources for reliability; gather and cite references in target language; use statistical data, quotations and research evidence; analyse overviews of contemporary issues from multiple source types.
wider: Conduct a research task using multiple target language sources — evaluate source quality, synthesise across perspectives, and produce a referenced summary with citations
Compare how sources are evaluated and cited in target language academic contexts with Australian English conventions — identify differences in citation format and credibility criteria

response_modes.reason: Source evaluation and citation require repeated practice across research tasks before the conventions become reliable. Regular research tasks with explicit citation requirements build the academic literacy skills the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students who access target language media can build research skills on existing consumption habits. Width investment here transforms passive media access into active, critical academic research practice.
success_criteria: Evaluates at least two sources using explicit reliability criteria
Cites at least one source appropriately in target language

nodes.label: Formal responses to contemporary issues
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create formal written or spoken responses to contemporary issues, applying formal text type knowledge and using evidence to develop an informed position.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a formal response to a contemporary issue of at least eight sentences, using at least two pieces of evidence and appropriate formal conventions.
nodes.typical_width: Apply understanding of news articles and formal text types to create responses to contemporary issues; produce formal written responses to current affairs; present analytical responses to documentary or interview texts; respond to First Nations Australian stories in target language with reflective personal response.
wider: Produce an extended analytical response to a contemporary issue — drawing on multiple sources, applying formal conventions, and evaluating the issue from multiple perspectives
Compare own formal response with a published target language commentary on the same issue — identify differences in structure, evidence use and rhetorical approach

response_modes.reason: Formal responses to contemporary issues integrate rhetorical analysis (node 1) and source evaluation (node 2) into a full analytical production task. The teaching investment is in creating genuine contemporary issues — real current affairs, real community concerns — that require authentic analytical engagement.

success_criteria: Produces a formal response of at least eight sentences using at least two pieces of evidence
Applies appropriate formal text conventions throughout
